tagline: An energy technology company transforming energy for progress
hero_kpi_rationale: Strong growth in the IET segment (+10%) driven by structural demand for natural gas (LNG +7% in 2025), low-carbon technologies, and data center solutions. Positive contrast with OFSE, which declined (-8%) due to cyclicality in drilling. Positions BKR on sustainable energy trends.

kpis.name: Total Revenue
kpis.explanation: Money earned from the sale of products and services.
kpis.description: Consolidated revenue of $27.7 billion in 2025, slightly down from 2024 ($27.8B), driven by IET but offset by OFSE declines.

kpis.name: Net Income
kpis.explanation: Profit after all expenses and taxes.
kpis.description: Net income of $2.6 billion in 2025, down 13% from 2024 ($3.0B), impacted by mark-to-market adjustments and transaction-related costs.
kpis.signal: Decline due to financial adjustments and lower volumes.

kpis.name: IET Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the Industrial and Energy Technology segment.
kpis.description: The IET segment grew revenue by $1.2 billion (+10%) in 2025, driven by gas equipment and services (GTE, GTS) and data center solutions.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in gas and low-carbon solutions.

kpis.name: OFSE Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the Oilfield Services and Equipment segment.
kpis.description: The OFSE segment declined by $1.3 billion (-8%) in 2025 across all regions, due to lower drilling activity and geopolitical tensions.
kpis.signal: Significant decline linked to lower upstream spending.

kpis.name: Gross Margin
kpis.explanation: Difference between revenue and cost of goods sold, expressed as a percentage.
kpis.description: Gross margin remained stable in 2025 due to cost optimization initiatives, productivity gains, and favorable product mix.

kpis.name: Capital Expenditures
kpis.explanation: Spending to acquire or upgrade physical assets.
kpis.description: Capex increased in 2025 to support IET growth, particularly in low-carbon technologies, hydrogen, geothermal, and gas infrastructure.
kpis.signal: Higher Capex to support new energy investments.

kpis.name: Headcount
kpis.explanation: Total number of employees in the company.
kpis.description: Approximately 58,000 employees in 2025, following partial divestitures and acquisitions (acquisition of CDC, divestiture of Precision Sensors).

kpis.name: IET Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the Industrial and Energy Technology segment.
kpis.description: The IET segment grew revenue by $1.2 billion (+10%) in 2025, driven by gas equipment and services (GTE, GTS) and rising demand for data center solutions.
kpis.signal: Strong growth in gas and low-carbon solutions.

kpis.name: OFSE Segment Revenue
kpis.explanation: Revenue from the Oilfield Services and Equipment segment.
kpis.description: The OFSE segment declined by $1.3 billion (-8%) in 2025 across all regions, due to lower drilling activity.
kpis.signal: Significant decline linked to lower upstream spending.

kpis.name: Dividend Per Share
kpis.explanation: Montant total versé en dividendes par action sur l'année fiscale. Indicateur clé pour les investisseurs orientés revenus.
kpis.description: 5-year history of declared dividends per share (2021-2025).

kpis.name: Capital Returned to Shareholders
kpis.explanation: Total annuel du cash redistribué aux actionnaires : dividendes versés + rachats d'actions (treasury stock).
kpis.description: For 2025: cumulative dividends + share buybacks in billions USD.

kpis.name: Payout Ratio
kpis.explanation: Part du bénéfice net redistribuée en dividendes. Au-dessus de 80 % indique un dividende potentiellement non-soutenable.
kpis.description: Dividends / net income for 2025 (based on net income attributable to shareholders).

kpis.name: RPO Backlog (Remaining Performance Obligations)
kpis.explanation: Visibilité revenu 2-3 ans, leadership IET sur LNG/datacenter power
kpis.description: 2-3 year revenue visibility, IET leadership in LNG/datacenter power

kpis.name: Free Cash Flow
kpis.explanation: Conversion FCF en hausse, finance dividendes + rachats
kpis.description: Rising FCF conversion, funds dividends and buybacks

kpis.name: IET Orders
kpis.explanation: Book-to-bill >1.0, exposition LNG/turbines AI data center
kpis.description: Book-to-bill >1.0, exposure to LNG/turbines AI data center

kpis.name: EBITDA Margin
kpis.explanation: Levier opérationnel IET, mix shift favorable
kpis.description: IET operating leverage, favorable mix shift

kpis.name: Dividend per Share
kpis.explanation: Hausse régulière dividende, signal confiance cash
kpis.description: Steady dividend growth, cash strength signal

risks.title: Competition
risks.score_rationale: The company operates in a highly competitive environment. The ability to maintain margins depends on technological differentiation and innovation capabilities relative to competitors. (Item 1A, OPERATIONAL RISKS)

risks.title: Energy Transition
risks.score_rationale: The company's success depends on the energy transition and demand for clean technologies (hydrogen, geothermal, CCUS). A slowdown in this transition would have a direct negative impact on IET growth.

risks.title: Supply Chain
risks.score_rationale: The company relies heavily on its supply chain, particularly for aero-derivative components. Supply chain disruptions can impact delivery timelines and operational execution.

risks.title: Oil and Gas Price Volatility
risks.score_rationale: Customer upstream spending is highly influenced by Brent and WTI oil prices. Lower prices in 2025 (Brent $69.14/bbl vs $80.52 in 2024) directly impacted OFSE (-8% revenue).

risks.title: Mergers and Acquisitions Risks
risks.score_rationale: The proposed acquisition of Chart carries risks: regulatory approvals (still pending in certain jurisdictions), potential failure to close, or failure to realize expected synergies. Expected close in Q2 2026.

risks.title: Loss of Key Personnel
risks.score_rationale: The ability to execute strategy depends on retaining key personnel and technical talent. Loss of critical employees could impact innovation and operational execution.

risks.title: Macroeconomic and Exploration Spending
risks.score_rationale: In 2025, global upstream spending declined due to geopolitical tensions, trade uncertainty, and concerns over additional OPEC+ supply. Demand for oilfield services is directly tied to exploration and development spending.

ai_positioning.summary: Baker Hughes identifies AI and data center expansion as a new structural driver of energy demand. Rising demand for data center growth is recognized as an additional driver of electricity and natural gas demand, particularly in the context of cooling and powering AI infrastructure.
evidence: AI and data center expansion adding a new structural layer of power demand
Growing emphasis on data centers within IET portfolio expansion
